From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next tests: private deployment & networking fallbacks

Thanks for the productive call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. High-level notes: 

- Goal: validate a Private (VPC) deployment for CloudScale's inference workload with an air-gapped / limited-egress control-plane option.
- Success criteria (from your side): end-to-end inference latency within 60ms p95 for 2k token average, control-plane calls limited to metadata-only (no customer payload), and ability to failover to hosted Redwood API within 250ms when local capacity is constrained.

Proposed next tests (attached test plan):
1) Network path verification: traceroutes from one of your staging subnets to our control-plane public IPs + an IPsec tunnel test if you prefer a VPN-based approach.
2) Control-plane reachability: verify that metadata-only handshakes work over a restricted egress policy.
3) Fallback behavior: simulate node exhaustion and measure failover latency to Redwood-hosted endpoint.
4) Quantization & kernel check: run a small model snippet (we'll share a q8 test binary) to confirm kernel compatibility on your instance types.

Attachments: private-test-plan.xlsx (has step-by-step commands plus expected telemetry), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf (high-level differentiators vs major hyperscalers).

Questions for you:
- Which staging subnet and IP we should use for the traceroute?
- Are you okay with a short iperf3 window for throughput characterization?

I suggest a 2-hour test window next Tuesday, 21 Jul (09:00-11:00 PT). If that works, we'll provision a temporary dedicated testing pool and send a DocuSign trial addendum to lock the window.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: private-test-plan.xlsx]

Sean — thanks for the summary and for pulling together the plan. This matches our internal notes. Quick answers: 

- Staging subnet: 10.40.2.0/24 (staging-az1). We can open a transient outbound rule for the test window.
- iperf3: ok for a short run. We prefer IPsec rather than a managed tunnel if possible for our security team.
- Air-gapped concern: our security lead wants explicit confirmation that the control plane will never receive request payloads (only pointers/metadata). Can you confirm?

Also, a competitor (one of the big hyperscalers) told us they can keep control-plane egress to a single IP range via their VPC endpoints. Curious how Redwood's private control-plane differs operationally and for audit logs. Could you include a short note on what telemetry you store and how it's accessible for SOC/audit?

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next tests: private deployment & networking fallbacks

Sean — quick technical draft below you can send to Asha verbatim. TL;DR: control plane is metadata-only, we never accept or persist customer request payloads on the control plane; payloads flow peer-to-peer to the runtime nodes and are encrypted in transit.

--- BEGIN TECH NOTE (send to CloudScale) ---
Control-plane behavior
- Control-plane only receives checklist and routing metadata: model id, model version, request size hint, customer nonces, and a signed pointer to the request location. No unencrypted request text is sent to the control plane.
- Telemetry and audit logs: we log control-plane handshake timestamps, model version, decision (route/dedicated/hosted), and anonymized request size buckets.
- Retention & access: control-plane logs retained 30 days by default for trial customers (configurable up to 365 days under enterprise contracts). Access to raw logs is gated via RBAC; audit exports available via S3-compatible signed URL for a given date range.

Network test recommendations
1) Traceroute from 10.40.2.10 -> control-plane IPs listed in the test plan.
2) IPsec tunnel: we support IKEv2; share your public endpoint and local subnets and we’ll provide transform sets.
3) Fallback verification: create an artificially constrained dedicated pool (2x T4 or equivalent) and spike traffic to trigger failover; measure client-side latency and token continuity.

Kernel/quant test
- We'll provide a small q8 model binary and a one-off docker image. Command: ./run_quant_check --model-snippet /tmp/q8.bin --sequence 2048. Expected output: kernel compatibility success + runtime latency approx.

--- END TECH NOTE ---

I can also run the kernel/quant test on a short remote session if they'd prefer.

Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer
